crop_processing.notes: All saved crops were visually inspected. Some saved crops and the original image were reopened for visual scope and letter checks; no additional crops were generated.

boxes.comments: The left alors has a horizontal cancellation across the complete word. The live right word has a tall looped l, low o, short r and terminal s followed by a separate descending comma. Its initial a is heavily overwritten: the low oval and right stem coexist with extra upper horizontal and vertical strokes. A complete independent older token and its chronology are not securely recoverable, so the doubt is confined to that live initial.

Both pi forms and their lower 1 indices, the left prime, both pairs of parentheses, the single right arrowhead, the separate wavy sign above its shaft, and the two equality bars are visible. The final current glyph has a two-lobed E outline with extra long parallel vertical strokes through or beside its lower bowl and a small dark lower-right point. The glyph is marked locally doubtful without supplying an older overwritten token. The smaller S index is clear. The curved E is rendered with mathcal from its visible form. No terminal punctuation is securely visible inside this box.

The compact sign at the left is crossed by oblique strokes. A long top bar, two lower legs and a small index-like lower upright favor pi_1, while the tangled lower strokes remain doubtful. The following current expression has two curved E forms, a branched lower K and smaller lower S. The connector has a plain left end and one small right head. No additional canceled token or terminal punctuation is supplied.

The article shows a tall closed l loop and low e return. The following sign has a detached upper horizontal bar and a lower component with a left cup, central cusp, long flat return and short right curl, read as barred compressed m. The sign is preserved rather than expanded into a word. A small low point far below the central sign is outside the reading scope.

The complete E_K-to-E_{S-prime} expression and following separate comma are included. The K has a stem and diagonal branches; the right S and its raised prime are visible. The horizontal connector begins plainly at the left. Its right end is rounded or slightly curled upward, without an independently isolated lower wing, so plain stroke and right arrow remain alternatives. The paper crease crossing the image is excluded from the ink reading.

The initial oval joins a low r arch and is followed by a separate comma. Its case is uncertain relative to the surrounding running text. The s and detached i dot are visible. The last word has a very compressed o and long flat n return with a downward terminal hook. All three words are complete within the box.

The word has an initial p stem with a long lower loop, compressed r/e bodies, a tall f with upper arch and lower loop, and a final low re sequence. A detached down-right stroke supports the grave on the second e. No securely separate acute can be isolated above the first e; the adjacent long rising stroke belongs to the f body. Only that first accent remains doubtful.

The raised word is attached by a curved leader at the left to the crossed baseline passage. Its tall f, looped e, low r and compressed m/e sequence support ferme with a separate short raised terminal accent, transcribed fermé. The baseline passage is canceled across its full visible extent; the initial downstroke and low joined bodies favor pro- but remain uncertain under the crossing and the added f descender. The final short lower horizontal stroke is retained with that tentative canceled reading. No revision chronology beyond canceled baseline plus raised insertion is supplied.

The complete visible line-end sequence has a long p descender, rounded o, low u and terminal r, followed by a separate short horizontal hyphen. Read literally pour-. No continuation from the next line is joined to it in this row.

The crop includes a complete visible line-opening t. fragment before the cancellation; its detached point is preserved. The following crossed word has a low first body and a higher final loop or arch, but horizontal and oblique cancellation strokes obscure the junctions. Tentative un and de remain alternatives for the whole canceled word. Both strike strokes cross that word; the preceding t. is outside their extent. No missing prefix is supplied for the line-opening fragment.

The first short word consists of two low joined bodies whose flattened forms leave ne/un unresolved. The long central word shows r/e/c/o/u/v/r followed by a small e, flattened n and a final t whose foot returns to the sloping baseline, supporting the literal full reading recouvrent. The final word has a long looped p descender and compressed a/s bodies, read pas. No punctuation is added. The right word is wholly inside the box.

The first word shows initial c, joined e/n, a short s and final e with a separate raised acute, read censé. The second shows s, dotted i, g with a long left-returning descender, low n/i, a tall f, another dotted i and compressed final e/r ending in a downward hook, read signifier. The descender entering from the upper crop edge belongs to the preceding line and is outside scope. No following word is completed.
Separate bottom-left foliation 70. The first numeral has a rising top, descending stem and crossbar; the second is a closed oval. It is preserved as margin content.
Head number 35. The first numeral has two curved lobes, and the second has a broad upper horizontal stroke and descending lower curve. Both are complete within the box.
Single numeral 1 with an oblique entry, long main stem and broad lower foot. It is an inline numeral, with no source parentheses or label punctuation in this box.

The relation has an upper right-pointing angle and a separate lower oblique bar, followed by a clear 2 with curved upper body and horizontal foot. A small separate solid point lies below the left part of the numeral foot. Its punctuation role is uncertain, so it is retained as a local doubtful period. The comma visible farther right on the original lies outside this frozen box and is not completed here.
